## Layout of the code {#sec-layout}

The numerical core is the Julia package `NestedMHD` in [`core/`](https://github.com/yipihey/NestedTurbulence/tree/main/core):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/physics.jl` | pointwise physics: conversions, fluxes, MonCen, Hancock, HLL/HLLD/LLF, GLM pair, GS05 EMF |
| `src/kernels.jl` | per-patch kernels: ghost filling on the root, reconstruction, fluxes, EMFs, cell and face updates, CFL |
| `src/interlevel.jl` | parent–child kernels: snapshot, prolongation, restriction, flux/EMF accumulation, reflux, EMF correction |
| `src/hierarchy.jl` | patch and hierarchy types, the recursive adaptive driver |
| `src/setup.jl` | initial conditions (vector potential), totals, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ diagnostics |
| `src/forcing.jl` | turbulence driving (finite Fourier modes in real space, OU amplitudes), isothermal reset, Mach feedback |
| `src/probe.jl` | one-cell time series streamed to a self-describing binary file, and its reader |
| `test/runtests.jl` | the validation suite cited by the ✓ badges |
| `bench/run_experiments.jl` | every dataset in this report and the laboratory except the next one |
| `bench/run_mach10.jl` | the driven Mach-10 run of @sec-ergo-run |

```julia
using NestedMHD
H = nested_central(32, 3; n=32, mode=:ct, riemann=:hll, T=Float32)   # 3 levels, 32³ each
init!(H, (x,y,z) -> (ρ, vx, vy, vz, p, Bx, By, Bz); vecpot = (x,y,z) -> (Ax, Ay, Az))
evolve!(H, 0.5)
level_summary(H); totals(H); max_divb(H)
```

Pass `backend = CUDABackend()` (or `MetalBackend()`, `ROCBackend()`) to `Hierarchy`/`nested_central`
to place every array on that device. The kernels are written once with `@kernel`.

## Data layout {#sec-data}

Every patch is a dense box with $g = 2$ ghost cells per side:

- `U[i,j,k,v]`: GLM stores the 9 conserved variables. CT stores 5 conserved variables plus the
  cell-centred field (derived from the faces after every face update).
- `bx[i,j,k]`: $B_x$ on the *lower* $x$-face of cell $(i,j,k)$; `by`, `bz` likewise (CT only).
- `F[i,j,k,c,d]`: flux component $c$ through the lower $d$-face. Each face is solved once and the
  array is kept until the parent has refluxed.
- `ex[i,j,k]` on the edge $(i, j-\tfrac12, k-\tfrac12)$, and cyclically (CT only).
- `rec[i,j,k,:]`: the Hancock half-step state, the three half-slopes, and (CT) the GS05 reference EMF.

Two ghost layers are enough for the CT edge EMFs on the patch-boundary edges, provided each kernel
runs over exactly the index range the next one needs: reconstruction on $[g, g+n+1]$, normal faces on
$[g+1, g+n+1]$ with transverse range $[g, g+n+1]$, edges on $[g+1, g+n+1]$. The comments in
`kernels.jl` give the derivation. A periodic root owns faces $g+1..g+n$ along each direction (face
$g+n+1$ is a copy of face $g+1$). A child owns $g+1..g+n+1$: its boundary faces are evolved by its own
EMFs and reconciled with the parent by the EMF correction (@sec-reflux).

## Kernels and their order {#sec-kernels}

One step of one patch launches, in order:

| Kernel | Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `periodic_cells_kernel!` / `prolong_faces_kernel!`, `prolong_cells_kernel!` | ghosts | root / child |
| `bcc_kernel!` | whole patch | CT: cell field from faces |
| `sig_kernel!` + `maximum` | interior | CFL reduction on the device |
| `copybox*_kernel!` | $[a-2, b+2]$ | snapshot, parents only |
| `recon_kernel!` | $[g, g+n+1]^3$ | slopes + Hancock (+ GS05 reference EMF) |
| `flux_kernel!` | $[g, g+n+1]^3$ | three lower faces per cell, Riemann solver selected at compile time |
| `emf_kernel!` | $[g+1, g+n+1]^3$ | CT only |
| `update_cells_kernel!`, `update_faces_kernel!` | interior / owned faces | in place (all fluxes computed first) |
| `accum_flux_kernel!`, `accum_emf_kernel!` | boundary surface | children only |

After a child has caught up, the parent runs `reflux_kernel!`, `emf_correct_kernel!` (CT),
`restrict_faces_kernel!` (CT), `restrict_cells_kernel!` and `bcc_kernel!`. Gathers are used instead of
scatters (every reflux or EMF-correction thread owns one output cell or face), so no kernel needs
atomics.

**Covered-region margins.** With $\mathrm{MU} = 2$, a parent skips: cell and face updates deeper than
MU inside the child's footprint, EMFs deeper than MU+1, fluxes deeper than MU+2, and reconstruction
deeper than MU+3. Shifting a cell by one in one direction changes its depth by at most one, so each
margin covers the stencil of the stage that reads it{{< src deep >}}. A switch turns skipping off
(`skip_covered=false`) and the test suite checks that skipping does not change the answer
{{< test "covered-region skipping" "same answer" >}}.

## What was kept from GLMMHDTurb, and what was not {#sec-kept}

**Kept**, because it is portable:

- the physics, line for line, made generic over `Float32`/`Float64` (every literal is `T(…)`, so
  `ifelse` never mixes types and nothing promotes in a `Float32` kernel);
- `@fastmath` + branchless `ifelse` in MonCen. This was GLMMHDTurb's decisive optimisation
  (398 → 993 Mcell/s): without it Julia's `min`/`max` keep their NaN semantics;
- `NTuple` states that live in registers, and the Riemann solver selected at compile time through `Val`;
- HLL as the default solver (branchless, two waves);
- each reconstruction computed once and each face solved once;
- $c_h$ from the CFL step and the HLLD guard of `sweep-fixes`.

**Changed**: GLMMHDTurb's tiled kernels write a second state buffer (`unew = uold + flux`). Here the
fluxes are kept in their own array for refluxing anyway, so the update is done in place.

**Not kept (yet)**: GLMMHDTurb's fastest kernels are CUDA-specific. They are shared-memory tiles in
Float16 with Float32 updates (1900 Mcell/s for GLM on an A6000), and `nvcc` line-marches driven from
Julia (3100 Mcell/s). They assume a periodic box indexed by wrap-around and record no fluxes.
NestedMHD's portable kernels use global-memory scratch for the reconstruction (36–39 values per cell)
and the fluxes (27 or 24), which is several times the memory traffic of the tiled kernels.
@sec-roadmap describes how the tiled kernel could be brought into a patch with flux export.

## Reproducing everything {#sec-repro}

```sh
cd core
julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate(); Pkg.test()'          # the validation suite (~3 min on 2 threads)
julia -t auto --project bench/run_experiments.jl                         # all datasets → ../app/data/*.json
julia -t auto --project bench/run_experiments.jl ghost convergence      # or a subset
```
